svg.title: Trace the parental X instead of guessing from sex
svg.desc: In the simplified fruit-fly X-linked recessive white-eye model, XᴿXᴿ female crossed with XʷY male gives red XᴿXʷ daughters and red XᴿY sons. Reversing the parental phenotypes gives XᴿXʷ red daughters and XʷY white sons. The first-cross F1 pairing XᴿXʷ×XᴿY yields XᴿXᴿ,XᴿXʷ,XᴿY,XʷY at one-quarter each with equal sex and gamete probabilities. White occurs in half the sons, one-quarter of all offspring. Paternal X goes to daughters and paternal Y to sons. A male-only pattern can also involve other inheritance models, sex-limited expression or chance; it is not unique proof of X linkage.

g.text: Trace the parental X instead of guessing from sex
Specified fruit-fly genotypes distinguish reciprocal crosses and conditional probabilities.
Fruit-fly eye-colour model: Xᴿ = red, Xʷ = white; red is dominant in XX flies.
Cross 1: XᴿXᴿ female × XʷY male → daughters XᴿXʷ; sons XᴿY (all red).
Reciprocal: XʷXʷ female × XᴿY male → daughters XᴿXʷ (red); sons XʷY (white).
F1 cross from Cross 1: XᴿXʷ female × XᴿY male
With equal sex probabilities: white is ½ among sons, ¼ among all offspring.
Father supplies X to daughters and Y to sons. Male-only observations alone do not prove X linkage.
